title: Inference field-doodles: kernels, rehearse tricks, and odd failure modes
content:
Quick, messy brain dump from the last two weeks of skimming papers + internal chat threads. Not polished — mostly for my future self and teammates who want fast entry points.

Context / why I care:
- We're seeing weird tail latency / quality tradeoffs when nodes fall back to smaller kernels under memory pressure. Not catastrophic but correlated with specific token patterns (long lists, code blocks, repeated delimiters).
- Want to capture plausible mechanisms and concrete experiments to isolate: is it numerical instability from quant fallback, KV-cache eviction order, or attention kernel path misselection?

Papers & notes (super short):
1) "Fallback-Aware Attention Kernels" (arXiv:2901.12345) — quick skim
- Idea: runtime chooses between full-fp and quantized kernels based on predicted activation magnitude distribution; includes a calibration pass using first N tokens.
- Found an example trace where switching mid-generation produced step-jumps in token logits (esp. at repeated punctuation).
- Takeaway: switching heuristic matters; calibration windows should avoid boundary tokens (end-of-sentence markers).
- Relevance: may explain sudden hallucination resets when falling back.

2) Engineering blog: "Prompt rehearsal for stable generations" (internal blog link copied into Confluence)
- Rehearsal = run a short prefix generation in a lightweight model to prime KV-cache / hidden-state distributions before hitting large sequence.
- Observed improved consistency in some internal evals for long-context summarization.
- Tradeoff: extra compute, plus risk of priming error. Possibly useful as a cheap mitigation when we detect kernel fallback.

3) KV eviction heuristics survey (notes from Confluence playbook)
- LRU vs time-decayed vs semantics-aware TTL. Eviction interacts with recompute costs (cache miss forces larger attention recompute).
- Hypothesis: interplay between eviction and quantized kernel selection could amplify small numerical diffs into divergent beams.

Open questions / hypotheses to test:
- H1: Kernel switching near structured delimiters ("\n", ``` code fences, long lists) causes discontinuities because calibration windows include those boundary tokens. Simple fix: forbid switch inside a fence or require a cool-down tokens window.
- H2: Eviction of older KV segments that contain grounding context causes the model to re-anchor to priors; if fallback kernel uses different normalization this magnifies drift.
- H3: Prompt rehearsal (1–3 tokens generated by a cheap model) can stabilize hidden activation statistics enough to reduce kernel oscillation frequency.

Quick experiments to run (priority ordering):
- E1: Reproduce with deterministic log capture. Create a micro-benchmark that forces fallback at token 150 with three prompt shapes (code fence, regular paragraph, list). Compare logits before/after switch. Link to PR template in GH. — Owner: Hui (me), collaborator: Mira.
- E2: Synthetic cache-eviction test: instrument KV entries with TTL tags, force eviction and compare next-token perplexities with/without quant kernel. — Owner: Oliver.
- E3: Prompt rehearsal A/B: insert 2 token rehearsal vs none for 1k long-context samples from summarization eval set. Measure BLEU/ROUGE/LL.

Notes from Slack thread (#kernel-weirdness):
- @mira noted a case where fallback occurred only on GPU type B. Could be kernel implementation path differences.
- @oliver measured a small but consistent logit-scale shift (~0.02) post-switch which amplified after 8 tokens.

Practical mitigations to try quickly (cheap):
- Prevent kernel switch if previously used kernel produced >N identical top-k tokens in last M steps (i.e., don't switch during a stable generation).
- Add a 4-token cool-down after any kernel switch before allowing another switch.
- If switch must happen, run a micro-calibration: run 4 token forward passes in the target kernel with cached past to align numeric stats (small compute overhead).

Longer-term ideas (researchy):
- Formalize a metric for "generation continuity" that looks at local logit trajectories and flags potential divergence at switch points. Could be used by rollout system to disable fallback for critical routes.
- Explore adaptive rehearsal that draws rehearsal tokens from a compressed summary of the recent KV cache rather than dummy tokens.

Unresolved questions for the group:
- Is there an existing perf/inference trace we can point to that matches the arXiv traces? I searched for JIRA-INF-1127 (linked above) because it contains one reproduction; needs triage.
- Do we have GPU-specific kernel differences documented across the fleet (NVIDIA vs AMD vs TPU) that might systematically bias fallback behavior?

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Create micro-benchmark harness (E1) — target: 2029-03-25
- [ ] Add kernel-switch cool-down flag to runtime (feature flag) — target: 2029-04-05
- [ ] Run prompt rehearsal A/B (E3) on 500 samples — target: 2029-04-09

References I should read/annotate next:
- "Numerical Stability in Low-bit Attention" (ICLR workshop paper, 2028) — priority
- "Cache-aware quantization plans" (internal notes, infra team) — loop in infra/Oliver

Random scribbles:
- Could we do rehearsal offline (pre-send) but store the resulting KV deltas as a lightweight patch? Then apply patch at runtime to reduce compute? Too hacky but interesting.
- If cool-down solves it 90% of the time, worth defaulting to cool-down on Hosted API until we root cause.

If you read this and have pointers / past repros, drop into #kernel-weirdness or ping me directly.

-- Hui
